title: Flaky Buttermilk Biscuits
subtitle: Gold-standard 23.6% butter ratio for tall, tender, flaky layers
instructions: Preheat oven to 218°C (425°F) and chill your mixing bowl.
Whisk flour, baking powder, sugar, and salt together until uniform.
Work or grate the ice-cold butter into the dry mix until flat, pea-sized flakes remain.
Pour in cold buttermilk and fold gently just until hydrated. Pat and fold the dough over itself 4 times to build flaky laminations.
Portion or stamp biscuits to your chosen biscuit count and gram weight. Bake at 218°C (425°F) for 15–20 minutes until tall and golden brown.
chefNotes: Selected the 23.6% butter-to-flour ratio (500g flour : 118g butter : 255g buttermilk), which matches King Arthur's benchmark for maximum lift without butter pooling.

title: King Arthur Soft Butter Buns
subtitle: Pillowy potato-flour & dry-milk burger or dinner buns

ingredients.name: Potato Flour or Instant Potato Flakes

instructions: Combine all dough ingredients and knead by hand or stand mixer until soft, supple, and smooth.
Place in a lightly greased bowl, cover, and let rise for 60–90 minutes until doubled.
Gently deflate and divide into your selected number of dough balls and gram weight. Shape each piece into a smooth taut ball.
Arrange in lightly greased cake pans or a 9"×13" pan, cover, and proof for 60–90 minutes until crowded and puffy. Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F).
Bake for 22–24 minutes until golden brown and the center registers 88°C (190°F). Brush immediately with melted butter.
chefNotes: Tip: Select 16 buns at 80g each on the sliders above to match your 650g flour batch automatically.

title: King Arthur Parker House Rolls
subtitle: Classic butter-folded potato dinner rolls with pull-apart crumb
instructions: Whisk milk and egg gently and warm slightly to take off the chill. Combine with flour, potato flakes, sugar, salt, yeast, and dough butter.
Knead 7–8 minutes by mixer (10 minutes by hand) until smooth and satiny.
Let rise in a greased bowl for 90 minutes until puffy (it expands most in the final 30 minutes).
Roll dough into rectangles, brush with melted butter, fold lengthwise with a 1/2" overhang, and cut into individual rolls (or portion by weight).
Arrange in a greased 9"×13" pan, cover, and proof 45–60 minutes. Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 20–25 minutes until golden, then brush with remaining melted butter.
chefNotes: Canonical King Arthur formula (100% flour, 63.1% milk, 11.9% butter, 13.9% egg, 12% potato). Bump the Roll Count slider to 32 for your 760g double batch.

title: Asian Bakery Milk Bread (Loaves or Rolls)
subtitle: Woks of Life feather-light Chinese bakery milk bread
instructions: Add milk, egg, sugar, flour, yeast, and salt to a stand mixer with a dough hook. Knead for 15 minutes until smooth and pulling away from the bowl sides.
Cover with a damp towel and proof in a warm spot for 1–2 hours until doubled.
Stir dough in the mixer for 5 minutes to knock out gas bubbles. Divide into 16 balls for rolls or 2 loaves.
Proof covered in greased pans for 1 hour. Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F).
Brush with egg wash and bake 23–25 minutes until golden. Brush immediately with simple syrup while hot.

title: 100% Milk English Muffin Bread (9×5 Loaf)
subtitle: No-knead batter loaf with crisp cornmeal crust and craggy interior
instructions: Grease a 9"×5" loaf pan and dust generously with cornmeal.
Warm milk to 49°C–54°C (120°F–130°F).
Combine dry ingredients, pour in warm milk and oil, and beat on high for 1 minute (or 3 minutes by hand).
Transfer to prepared pan and let rise until crowning 1/4 inch above the rim.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) until internal temperature hits 88°C (190°F), tenting loosely with foil at 20 minutes if browning rapidly.

title: Skillet Griddle English Muffins
subtitle: Semolina-dusted stovetop English muffins cooked on cast iron
instructions: Combine lukewarm milk, sugar, yeast, bread flour, salt, and softened butter. Knead 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in an oiled bowl for 1–1.5 hours until doubled.
Divide into equal portions according to your muffin count and gram weight, shape into balls, flatten into 2.5cm disks on a semolina-dusted sheet, and dust tops.
Proof 30–45 minutes until puffy, then cook on a dry heavy skillet over medium-low heat for 6–8 minutes per side until 93°C (200°F) inside.
Cool on a wire rack and fork-split to preserve nooks and crannies.

title: New York Style Bagels (60% Hydration)
subtitle: Ethan Chlebowski's chewy malt/honey-poached bagels
instructions: Bloom yeast and honey in 300g warm water for 5 minutes. Mix with bread flour and salt into a stiff mass; cover and rest 15 minutes.
Knead vigorously for 8–10 minutes until smooth and passing the windowpane test. Bulk ferment 45 minutes until doubled.
Divide into equal balls using your chosen bagel count and gram weight, shape rings, and proof 45–60 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).
Boil in the honey-baking soda water bath for 30–60 seconds per side, brush with egg wash, top with Everything seasoning, and bake at 246°C (475°F) for 12–15 minutes.

title: Soft Yogurt & Garlic Naan Flatbread
subtitle: Tender yogurt-enriched skillet flatbreads
instructions: Bloom yeast and sugar in lukewarm water for 5–10 minutes.
Mix in oil, yogurt, flour, salt, and baking soda; knead into a soft, smooth dough and let rise 1 hour.
Divide into equal dough balls, roll thin, and sear on a dry cast-iron skillet until bubbly and blistered.

title: Homemade Real-Potato Burger Buns
subtitle: Soft burger buns enriched with mashed potato, butter, and dry milk
instructions: Knead all ingredients into a smooth, elastic dough and bulk ferment 60–90 minutes until doubled.
Portion into your selected bun count and gram weight, shape into tight rounds, and proof 45–60 minutes.
Bake at 180°C (355°F) for 15–20 minutes until golden.

title: Sonoran-Style Flour Tortillas (Manteca / Lard)
subtitle: Canonical 18.8% lard, 62.5% hydration formula for soft, pliable tortillas
instructions: Whisk flour, salt, and baking powder. Rub in lard until fine crumbs form.
Pour in warm/hot water and knead 4–5 minutes until smooth and supple.
Divide into equal dough balls using your chosen count and gram weight; cover and rest 15 minutes.
Roll thin and cook on a hot dry comal or cast-iron skillet for 30–45 seconds per side until blistered.

title: Artisan Sourdough / Poolish Pizza Dough (13" Pies)
subtitle: 62.2% hydration King Arthur Bread / Caputo pizza formula

ingredients.name: King Arthur Bread Flour or Caputo

instructions: Dissolve poolish and IDY in filtered water, mix in flour, autolyse 20 minutes, and knead in salt.
Perform stretch-and-folds, bulk ferment, then divide into your selected number of pies and gram weight per dough ball.
Cold-ferment 24–48 hours before stretching and baking at maximum oven/steel temperature.

title: Students Pizza Dough with Wheat Biga
subtitle: 75% Bread Flour / 25% Cake Flour blend with whole-wheat biga pre-ferment
yieldText: 23 dough balls at 298g each (6,844g total dough)
instructions: Ferment the Wheat Biga (400g whole wheat flour + 400g water + 2g yeast) ahead of time.
Mix bread flour, cake flour, 200g ripe biga, cold water, and sea salt.
Portion into dough balls using your chosen count and weight above and ferment 48–72 hours.

title: Homemade Copycat Fritos Corn Chips
subtitle: Crispy nixtamalized Masa Harina corn chips with Japan sourcing notes

ingredients.name: Masa Harina (Nixtamalized Corn Flour / マサ粉)

instructions: Knead masa harina, salt, and warm water for 2–3 minutes until smooth like Play-Doh. Rest 10 minutes covered.
Roll between plastic wrap to 1.0–1.5mm thin and slice into 1.2cm × 5cm ribbons.
Fry in corn or canola oil at 175°C–180°C (350°F) for 60–90 seconds until golden. Drain and salt immediately.

title: Bull's-Eye Hickory Smoke BBQ Sauce
subtitle: Rich ketchup, Worcestershire, butter, brown sugar & liquid smoke glaze
instructions: Combine all ingredients in a heavy saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk until butter melts and sugar dissolves.
Bring to a gentle bubble and simmer on low for 15 minutes until glossy and thickened.
chefNotes: Tap Half (½×) for your 117g ketchup batch or Generous (1½×) for your 352g ketchup extra batch.

title: Tony Roma's Copycat Redemptively Sweet BBQ Sauce
subtitle: Honey-rich slow-reduced smokehouse rib glaze
instructions: Whisk all ingredients together in a saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for 30 to 40 minutes to reduce and thicken into a sticky glaze.

title: Dennis Marks' Chipotle-Molasses Emulsified BBQ Sauce
subtitle: Smoky chipotle in adobo, coconut molasses, lime juice & honey blended smooth
instructions: Add all ingredients (except honey) to a pot and simmer for ~20 minutes to desired consistency.
Let cool for 15 minutes, then stir in 1 tbsp honey.
Pour into a blender and emulsify until completely smooth.

title: Jeff's Original Naked Rib Rub
subtitle: Brown sugar & Hungarian paprika dry rub for pork ribs, brisket, chicken & fish
instructions: In a shallow dish or Ziploc bag, blend the dark brown sugar and paprika first, working out all lumps.
Add remaining spices one at a time, mixing thoroughly after each addition.
Store airtight in the freezer to keep brown sugar fresh and clump-free.
chefNotes: For milder heat, omit the cayenne and reduce coarse black pepper to 1 tbsp.

title: Carne Asada Dry Seasoning Blend
subtitle: Gram-weighed chili, garlic, Mexican oregano, cumin & crystallized lime

ingredients.name: Crystallized Lime Powder or Dried Lime Zest

instructions: Whisk all dry spices together in a small bowl until evenly distributed.
Rub generously onto skirt or flank steak with a splash of oil and fresh lime or orange juice before grilling.

title: Homemade Tapatío Copycat Hot Sauce (Japan-Pantry Edition)
subtitle: Engineered with Japanese Takanotsume & Korean Gochugaru for authentic Tapatío flavor

ingredients.name: Korean Coarse Red Pepper (Gochugaru / 韓国唐辛子 粗挽き)

instructions: Toast stemmed Takanotsume pods in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 30–45 seconds until fragrant.
Simmer toasted Takanotsume, Gochugaru, crushed garlic, and 350ml water covered for 10–12 minutes until softened.
Transfer hot mixture to a blender with vinegar, oregano, cumin, black pepper, and salt. Puree on high for 2–3 minutes.
Strain (uragoshi) through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing firmly with a ladle.
Return strained sauce to blender on low, sprinkle in 1/8 tsp xanthan gum, and blend 15–20 seconds. Bottle and chill 24–48 hours.

title: In-N-Out Animal-Style Burger Spread
subtitle: 62% mayo, 23% ketchup, 15% sweet pickle relish formula
instructions: Whisk mayonnaise, ketchup, sweet pickle relish, vinegar, sugar, and paprika together in a bowl until uniform.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before spreading on toasted burger buns.

title: Thai Suki Sauce (Roasted Peanut & Cilantro Chili Dip)
subtitle: Savory-tangy soy, lime, ginger, garlic, cilantro & ground peanut dipping sauce
yieldText: 1 standard bowl (~508g) — tap 1.5× for your handwritten parenthesis batch

ingredients.name: Sliced Thai Chili Peppers or Red Jalapeño

instructions: Whisk soy sauce, white vinegar, fresh lime juice, Tabasco, sugar, and sesame oil until sugar dissolves.
Stir in finely chopped ginger, garlic, cilantro leaves, ground roasted peanuts, and sliced Thai chili peppers.
chefNotes: Your email printout has (1.5×) numbers written in parentheses next to each line—just click the 'Generous (1½×)' preset button above to get those exact numbers!

title: Kansai-Style Yakitori Tare Glaze (関西風焼き鳥のタレ)
subtitle: Balanced maroyaka sweet-savory soy, hon-mirin, sake & charred negi reduction
instructions: Boil Off Alcohol: Combine sake and mirin in a small saucepan and boil over medium heat for 1–2 minutes.
Combine & Season: Lower heat to medium-low. Stir in soy sauce, sugar, and optional chicken bouillon until dissolved. Add charred green onion top and ginger.
Simmer & Reduce: Simmer gently for 12–18 minutes until reduced by 1/3 to 1/2 and coating the back of a spoon.
Cool & Strain: Discard green onion and ginger. Cool completely and store in an airtight jar in the fridge for up to 2–3 months.

title: Kansai-Style Savory Gyoza no Tare
subtitle: Gram-calibrated dashi, shoyu, rice vinegar & mirin dumpling dipping sauce
instructions: Whisk all ingredients together in a small bowl until the sugar and dashi dissolve.
Optional: add finely grated fresh ginger, rayu chili oil, or a drop of lemon juice.

title: Tentsuyu (Classic 4:1:1 Tempura Dipping Sauce)
subtitle: Traditional dashi, soy sauce & mirin dipping broth served with grated daikon
instructions: Combine dashi stock, soy sauce, and mirin in a saucepan.
Heat over medium just until it begins to boil to cook off the mirin alcohol.
Remove from heat and serve warm or at room temperature with grated daikon radish.

title: Pietro-Style Grated Onion & Sesame Salad Dressing
subtitle: 310g gram-accurate copycat of the famous Japanese restaurant dressing
instructions: Whisk or blend soy sauce, rice vinegar, grated onion, garlic, mirin, sugar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper.
Slowly whisk in vegetable oil and toasted sesame oil to emulsify, then stir in toasted sesame seeds.

title: Creamy Deli Coleslaw & Dressing
subtitle: Gram-calibrated mayonnaise, lemon juice & white vinegar slaw for 600g cabbage
yieldText: Full batch for 600g cabbage (tap Half ½× for your 300g cabbage Google Doc)
instructions: Whisk mayonnaise, sugar, lemon juice, white vinegar, kosher salt, and black pepper in a large mixing bowl until smooth.
Fold in the 600g shredded cabbage and carrot mix until evenly coated.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving so flavors meld.

title: Classic Buttermilk Ranch Dressing
subtitle: Equal-parts mayo, sour cream & buttermilk with dill, chives, parsley & lemon
instructions: Whisk mayonnaise, sour cream, and buttermilk together until smooth.
Stir in herbs, spices, salt, pepper, and fresh lemon juice to taste. Chill 30 minutes before serving.

title: Homemade Italian Dressing Dry Mix & Vinaigrette
subtitle: Gram-weighed dry herb blend plus prepared oil-and-vinegar dressing ratio
yieldText: 48.9g dry mix (~2 batches of prepared dressing)

ingredientGroups.groupName: To Prepare 1 Cruet of Liquid Dressing

instructions: Mix all dry ingredients together and store in a tightly sealed jar.
To prepare dressing: whisk together 1/4 cup white vinegar, 2/3 cup oil, 2 tbsp water, and 2 tbsp of the dry mix.

title: Caramelized French Onion Dip
subtitle: Creamy sour cream, cottage cheese, yogurt & mayo dip with sauteed onions

ingredients.name: Salt (total)
ingredients.volumeText: 1/4 tsp for onions + 1/2 tsp for base

instructions: Sauté chopped onion in olive oil with 1/4 tsp salt until soft and golden. Let cool.
Blend or whisk cottage cheese, sour cream, yogurt, mayonnaise, and seasonings until smooth, then fold in the cooked onions.

title: Lemon-Zest & Fresh Basil Olive Oil Drizzle (Caprese)
subtitle: Bright citrus-herb dressing for sliced tomatoes and fresh mozzarella

ingredients.name: Flaky Sea Salt & Cracked Black Pepper

instructions: Slice tomatoes and mozzarella into rounds, arrange on a platter, and pre-salt the tomatoes for 2–3 minutes so they release natural juices.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, and lemon zest until lightly emulsified; stir in basil and red pepper flakes.
Spoon over the platter and finish with flaky sea salt and black pepper.

title: Tony Gemignani's NY Pizza Sauce
subtitle: Uncooked crushed whole tomato & heavy puree New York pizzeria sauce
instructions: Crush the whole tomatoes by hand or pulse briefly, then whisk in the tomato puree, sea salt, oregano, onion powder, and black pepper.

title: Quick Pan-Deglaze Hamburg Steak Sauce
subtitle: Classic Japanese red wine, ketchup, tonkatsu/chunou & butter pan glaze
instructions: In the skillet used to cook the hamburg steaks, add red wine, water, ketchup, tonkatsu/chunou sauce, and butter.
Simmer 2–3 minutes while scraping up the fond until glossy.

title: In-N-Out Double-Double, Animal-Style (The Burger Lab)
subtitle: Kenji López-Alt's mustard-grilled 2oz patties, fondue caramelized onions & Spread
sourceFile: 03_Mains_and_Meats/The Burger Lab_ The Ins-n-Outs of an In-N-Out Double-Double, Animal-Style _ Serious Eats.html
yieldText: 4 Double-Double burgers (8 patties at 57g / 2 oz each)

ingredients.name: Kosher Salt & Freshly Cracked Black Pepper

instructions: Make the Fondue Onions: Slowly cook finely diced onions in oil over medium-low heat; each time they brown, deglaze with 2 tbsp water and repeat until dark, sweet, and jammy.
Whisk the Spread ingredients (mayonnaise, ketchup, relish, vinegar, and sugar) together.
Form ground chuck into thin 4-inch patties (57g / 2 oz each; 2 patties per Double-Double). Season generously with salt and pepper.

Toast buns deeply on a hot skillet. Sear patties on one side for 2 minutes, squirt yellow mustard onto the raw top side, flip so the mustard sizzles into the griddle for 1 minute, and top each patty with American cheese.
Spoon caramelized onions onto one cheesy patty, stack the second cheesy patty on top, and place on a bottom bun layered with 2 tbsp Spread, 4 pickle chips, tomato, and iceberg lettuce.

title: Japanese Hamburg Steak with Rich Onion Gravy
subtitle: 70:30 beef-pork patties with caramelized onion split between meat and pan gravy
yieldText: 10 standard patties (~173g raw each) or 8 large patties (~216g each)

ingredientGroups.groupName: 2. Hamburg Meat Mixture (1 kg Meat Scale)

ingredients.name: Ground Beef & Pork Mix (70% Beef : 30% Pork)
Cooled Fried Onion (2/3 of cooked onions)
Reserved Fried Onion (1/3 of cooked onions)

instructions: Sauté 800g diced onions in 20g oil until soft and golden (~495g cooked weight). Cool completely, then divide: 330g for the meat and 165g for the gravy.
Soak 60g panko in 124g milk for 3 minutes. Knead 1,000g meat and 8g salt in a chilled bowl until pale and sticky.
Mix in pepper, nutmeg, soaked panko, eggs, and 330g cooled onions. Divide into patties according to your count and weight settings, slap between hands to remove air pockets, and dimple the centers.
Sear patties in 15g oil over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes until golden, flip, cover with a lid, and steam-cook on low for 7–8 minutes until 74°C (165°F) internal temp.
Remove patties and deglaze the skillet with the reserved 165g fried onions, 200g water, 105g soy sauce, 75g mirin, and 18g grated garlic. Simmer 2–3 minutes, turn off heat, and swirl in 40g butter.

title: Authentic Japanese Scratch-Roux Beef Curry
subtitle: Single-pot scratch curry roux with beef komagire, caramelized onions & secret condiments
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and sauté sliced onions for 10 minutes until caramelized and lightly browned.
Add garlic paste and beef; cook until beef changes color, then toss in potatoes and carrots for 1–2 minutes.
Stir in 24g curry powder and toast 30–60 seconds until fragrant. Lower heat, add flour, and stir constantly for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in 1,400g water in two additions to prevent lumps, add bouillon cubes, cover, and simmer 15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and pepper; simmer uncovered 3 minutes until thickened, then finish with milk and salt.

title: Hard Rock Cafe Copycat Tupelo Chicken Tenders & 3 Sauces
subtitle: Spicy cornflake-crusted chicken tenders (1 kg scale) with Honey Mustard, Apricot & BBQ sauces
sourceFile: 03_Mains_and_Meats/Hard Rock Cafe Tupelo chicken tenders & sauce/Recipe.odt

ingredientGroups.groupName: 3. Quick Whisk Smokehouse BBQ Dipping Sauce

ingredients.name: Garlic Powder, Onion Powder & Black Pepper

instructions: Whisk the dipping sauces in separate bowls and chill.
Set up 3 dredge bowls: Bowl 1 (125g flour), Bowl 2 (240g milk + 100g eggs), Bowl 3 (100g coarse cornflake crumbs + all spices).
Double-dredge tenders: Flour (Bowl 1) → Egg Wash (Bowl 2) → Flour (Bowl 1) → Egg Wash (Bowl 2) → press firmly into Seasoned Cornflakes (Bowl 3).
Deep-fry in 5–8cm oil at 180°C (356°F) in batches of 4–5 tenders for 3–4 minutes until golden and 74°C (165°F) inside.

title: Southern Buttermilk Fried Chicken (Drumelets)
subtitle: Spiced buttermilk marinated drumelets with craggy katakuriko-flour crust
instructions: Whisk buttermilk, hot sauce, salt, and egg; submerge drumelets and marinate 2–8 hours.
Whisk flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and spices. Drizzle 2–3 tbsp marinade into the flour and toss with a fork to form craggy flakes.
Press drumelets firmly into the dredge, rest 10–15 minutes on a wire rack, and fry at 175°C (350°F) for 8–10 minutes (maintaining 155°C–165°C) until 74°C (165°F) at the bone.

title: Southern Buttermilk Fried Chicken (Boneless Thighs)
subtitle: Juicy palm-sized boneless thigh cutlets with double-dredged crunchy crust
instructions: Marinate halved boneless thighs in buttermilk, hot sauce, salt, and egg for 1–4 hours.
Whisk dredge ingredients, drizzle in 3–4 tbsp marinade to form flakes, press chicken into flour, and rest 10–15 minutes on a rack.
Fry at 175°C (350°F) for 6–8 minutes flipping halfway until deep golden and 74°C (165°F) internal temp.

title: Nagoya-Style Yamachan Tebasaki (Crispy Pepper Wings)
subtitle: Double-fried chicken wings brushed with reduced garlic-shoyu-mirin-honey glaze & white pepper
instructions: Simmer soy sauce, mirin, sake, honey, sesame seeds, and grated garlic in a small pan until reduced by half. Set aside.
Season wings with salt and pepper, then toss in equal parts cornstarch and cake flour.
First Fry: Fry at 160°C (320°F) for 3 minutes per side.
Second Fry: Raise oil to 190°C (374°F) and flash-fry 1 minute per side until shattering crisp.
Brush hot wings generously with the reduced tare and dust heavily with fine white pepper.

title: Crispy-Skin Chicken with Sun-Dried Tomato Cream Sauce
subtitle: Pan-seared bone-in chicken thighs roasted in garlic-Parmesan-basil cream sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 204°C (400°F). Season chicken thighs with kosher salt and black pepper.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a large oven-proof skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down 2–3 minutes per side until golden; set aside.
Melt remaining 1 tbsp butter, sauté garlic and red pepper flakes for 1–2 minutes, then stir in chicken broth, heavy cream, sun-dried tomatoes, Parmesan, thyme, oregano, and dried basil.
Simmer 3–5 minutes until slightly thickened, return chicken to skillet, and roast in oven for 25–30 minutes until 79°C (175°F) internal temperature. Garnish with fresh basil.

title: Juicy Sasami (Chicken Tenderloin) Fajitas
subtitle: Citrus-cumin-smoked paprika marinated chicken tenderloins with 3 cooking methods

ingredients.name: Chicken Tenderloins (Sasami / ささみ, tendons removed)

instructions: Remove the white tendon (suji) from each sasami using the fork-pull method and slice diagonally into 1.5–2cm strips.
Marinate chicken strips in olive oil, lime juice, garlic, and spices for 20–30 minutes at room temp (do not exceed 2 hours).
Sauté sliced peppers and onions over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes until charred and crisp-tender; remove to a bowl.
Flash-sear chicken strips in a single layer for 90 seconds per side (or air-fry at 200°C for 6–8 minutes) until 74°C (165°F). Toss back with veggies and serve in warm tortillas.

title: Chinese Restaurant Velvety Chicken & Bell Pepper Stir-Fry
subtitle: 1 kg egg-white velveted chicken tenderloin with bell peppers, onions & oyster-Shaoxing glaze
instructions: Coat chicken strips in soy sauce, sesame oil, egg white, cornstarch, and oil for 15–30 minutes.
Whisk all stir-fry sauce ingredients together in a bowl.
Velvet chicken in 1 tbsp hot oil in a wok over high heat until 80% cooked (white outside); remove and set aside.
Stir-fry garlic and ginger for 10 seconds, then toss in onions and bell peppers for 2–3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return chicken to the wok, pour in the sauce, and toss 1–2 minutes until glossy and thickened.

title: Easy Honey Garlic Glazed Pork Chops
subtitle: Pan-seared pork chops basted in a 4-ingredient caramelized honey-garlic-vinegar reduction

ingredients.name: Rice Wine or Apple Cider Vinegar

instructions: Season pork chops with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. Sear in hot oil over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes per side; transfer to a plate.
Melt butter in the same pan, sauté minced garlic for 30 seconds, and add honey, water/broth, and vinegar.
Simmer 3–4 minutes until reduced and syrupy, return pork chops to the pan to coat, and broil 1–2 minutes for caramelized edges.

title: Dennis Marks' Smoked Pork Ribs (3-2-1 Bend-Test Method)
subtitle: 225°F Big Green Egg / smoker method with mustard binder, honey foil wrap & bend test

ingredients.name: Dry Rib Rub (Jeff's Naked Rib Rub)

instructions: Peel silver skin off the back of the ribs using pliers. Coat with yellow mustard and dry rub the night before; wrap and refrigerate.
Smoke at 225°F (107°C) using the smoker plate for 3 hours (do not apply BBQ sauce early or sugar will burn).
Wrap each rack tightly in foil with 2–3 tbsp honey squirted over the top. Cook wrapped for 2 hours (in smoker or oven at 225°F).
Unwrap, baste both sides with BBQ sauce, and return to racks for 45–60 minutes.

Apply the Bend Test every 15 minutes: grab near the center with tongs—ribs pass when they bend 90 degrees and the meat surface begins to crack. Double-wrap in foil and rest in a cooler for 20 minutes.

title: Artisan Mexican Chorizo Sausage (By Weight & Baker's %)
subtitle: Pasilla, New Mexico & Ancho chile pork sausage calibrated by exact meat percentages
yieldText: Normalized to 1,000g (1 kg) pork using your exact butcher-paper percentages (scale up to 9,080g for full 20 lb batch)

ingredients.name: Ground Bay Leaves
ingredients.volumeText: ~1 bay leaf ground per kg (8 per 20 lbs)

instructions: Chill ground pork to 1°C–3°C (34°F–38°F).
Whisk all measured spices, chiles, and salt together, then knead thoroughly into the chilled pork until tacky.
Refrigerate overnight for flavors to meld before frying loose or stuffing into casings.
chefNotes: Transcribed from your Mexican Chorizo Sausage butcher-paper photo and normalized to 1,000g pork so you can easily make 500g or 1kg home batches!

title: English-Style Herbed Pork Breakfast Sausage
subtitle: Gram-accurate sage, thyme, marjoram & nutmeg pork sausage patties or links
instructions: Hydrate fine breadcrumbs with 30g cold water.
Mix chilled ground pork, hydrated breadcrumbs, salt, white pepper, sage, thyme, marjoram, and nutmeg until sticky.
Portion into patties or links using your chosen count and weight above and pan-fry over medium heat until golden brown.

title: Slow-Baked Stuffed Cabbage Rolls
subtitle: Tender cabbage leaves stuffed with spiced beef, pork & rice in rich tomato broth

ingredients.name: Black Pepper, Smoked Paprika & Dried Oregano
Sugar, Salt, Black Pepper & Dried Basil
ingredients.volumeText: 1 tsp sugar + 1/2 tsp each salt, pepper, basil

instructions: Core cabbage and parboil in boiling water for 2–3 minutes; peel off 12 softened leaves and trim thick stems.
Mix ground meat, cooled rice, onion, garlic, egg, salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and oregano.
Place filling in each leaf, fold in sides, and roll tightly.
Sauté sauce onion and garlic in olive oil, add crushed tomatoes, paste, beef broth, Worcestershire, and seasonings; simmer 5–10 minutes.
Layer rolls seam-side down over sauce in a heavy covered pot, pour remaining sauce on top, cover tightly, and bake at 150°C (300°F) for 3 hours.

title: Red Lobster Copycat Rock Shrimp Creole (Metric)
subtitle: 907g rock shrimp simmered in a spicy butter-roux tomato Creole sauce

ingredients.name: Cooked White or Wild Rice (for serving)

instructions: Melt 28.5g butter in a saucepan, stir in 16g flour to make a roux, then add 411g tomatoes with juice, sugar, salt, cayenne, and black pepper. Simmer until thickened and hold warm.
In a large skillet, melt remaining 28.5g butter over medium-high heat and sauté bell pepper, onion, celery, and garlic until tender-crisp.
Add 907g rock shrimp and cook ~3 minutes until opaque.
Pour in warm tomato Creole mixture, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer 5 minutes. Serve over hot rice.

title: Crispy Beer-Battered Fish & Chips
subtitle: Cornstarch dry dredge + carbonated beer batter fried at 190°C
instructions: Dredge dry fish fillets thoroughly in the cornstarch-flour-salt mixture and shake off excess.
Whisk flour, baking powder, paprika, and ice-cold beer together just until combined.
Dip dredged fish into the beer batter and fry at 190°C (375°F) for 5 to 8 minutes until golden and crisp.

title: Golden Buttermilk Corn Dogs
subtitle: Gram-calibrated cornmeal & buttermilk dipping batter fried at 180°C
yieldText: 10 to 12 large corn dogs (749g batter) — slide count to 15 for your 15-wiener batch
instructions: Whisk dry ingredients (cornmeal, flour, baking powder, sea salt, sugar) together.
Whisk in egg, vegetable oil, and buttermilk until smooth. Pour into a tall drinking glass for easy dipping.
Skewer dried wieners, dip into the batter, and fry at 180°C (356°F) for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden brown.

title: Costco Copycat High Roller Turkey Bacon Pinwheels
subtitle: Lavash flatbread roll-ups with Ranch cream cheese spread, turkey, bacon, Swiss & greens
instructions: Beat softened cream cheese, mayonnaise, Ranch seasoning, and chives until smooth.
Spread edge-to-edge over all 4 lavash flatbreads.
Layer cheese slices, turkey breast, crispy bacon, deseeded diced tomatoes, and dry greens.
Roll tightly into logs, wrap in plastic wrap, and chill 30–60 minutes before slicing into 1-inch pinwheels with a serrated knife.

title: Katsudon Dashi-Shoyu Simmering Sauce
subtitle: Gram-exact donburi broth for simmering crispy tonkatsu with egg & onion
instructions: Whisk water, dashi powder, brown sugar, shoyu, and mirin together.
Simmer sliced onion in half the broth per bowl, lay sliced tonkatsu on top, pour beaten egg around the cutlet, cover for 60 seconds until softly set, and slide over hot steamed rice.

title: Restaurant-Style Pork Fried Rice (Gram-Calibrated)
subtitle: Calibrated for 682g cooked cold rice (2 house cups / 310g raw rice)
yieldText: 682g cold rice batch (use the Cold White Rice slider below to scale to any leftover rice weight!)
instructions: Scramble beaten eggs in 1 tbsp shimmering oil into soft curds; remove immediately to a clean plate.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger, and scallion whites in high-heat oil for 20 seconds, then toss in mixed vegetables for 2–3 minutes.
Push veggies aside, sear diced cooked pork for 1–2 minutes until crispy at the edges, then add the cold rice and press against the hot wok for 2–3 minutes.
Return eggs to the wok, pour in soy sauce, oyster sauce, white pepper, sugar, and Shaoxing wine, and toss over high heat for 1–2 minutes.
Remove from heat and finish with toasted sesame oil and dark green scallion tops.
chefNotes: Tip: Drag the 'Cold Cooked White Rice' slider directly to match whatever weight of leftover rice is on your scale!

title: Festive Chirashizushi (Scattered Sushi Rice)
subtitle: Seasoned dashi-simmered shiitake, aburaage & carrots folded into sushi rice with kinshi tamago
instructions: Simmer sliced shiitake, aburaage, carrots, and optional renkon in 800ml dashi stock with sake, sugar, shoyu, and salt until tender; drain well.
Whisk eggs with 1/2 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt per egg, cook into thin crepes, and slice into fine ribbons (kinshi tamago).
Fold the drained simmered vegetables into warm sushi rice and top generously with the shredded egg.

title: Verified Authentic Mexican Red Rice
subtitle: Toasted white rice simmered with tomato, garlic & chicken bouillon (Verified June 20, 2020)
instructions: Toast 315g rice in 4 tbsp canola oil over medium heat until golden and nutty.
Blend or crush 200g tomato with 2 garlic cloves, 2 tbsp chicken bouillon, and 630ml water.
Pour into the toasted rice, bring to a boil, cover tightly, and simmer on low for exactly 17 minutes. Rest 5–10 minutes off heat before fluffing.

title: Classic Butter & Onion Rice Pilaf
subtitle: Gram-calibrated 200g basmati/jasmine rice toasted in butter with onion, garlic & bay leaf
instructions: Rinse rice under cold water until clear and drain well.
Melt 30g butter in a pot over medium heat and sauté 50g diced onion (and optional garlic) for 2–3 minutes until soft.
Add drained rice and toast 2–3 minutes until lightly golden.
Pour in 500g hot water with dissolved bouillon cube, add bay leaf, bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low for 15 minutes.
Rest covered off heat for 10 minutes, fluff with a fork, and fold in fresh parsley.

title: From-Scratch Pinto Beans: Boil to Creamy Refried Beans
subtitle: 500g dried pinto beans slow-simmered and emulsified with lard/oil, onion, garlic & cumin

ingredients.name: Salt (added in final 15 mins of boil)
Pork Lard, Bacon Fat, or Neutral Oil

instructions: Soak 500g rinsed pinto beans in 3× water with 10g salt for 8–12 hours (or quick-boil 2 minutes and rest covered 1 hour). Drain.
Cover beans by 3–5cm with fresh water, add halved onion and crushed garlic, and simmer gently for 60–90 minutes until tender, adding 1 tsp salt in the last 15 minutes. Reserve 1–2 cups bean broth!
Heat 2–3 tbsp lard or oil in a skillet, cook chopped onion until golden, and add minced garlic and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add drained beans, mash with a potato masher, and gradually splash in reserved bean liquid over medium-low heat until creamy and spreadable.

title: Quick Mexican-Style Refried Beans (Canned Mixed Beans)
subtitle: 15-minute refried beans adapted for a 400g can of mixed beans with bloomed spices

ingredients.name: Lard, Bacon Drippings, or Neutral Oil

instructions: Drain can of beans, reserving 3–4 tbsp canning liquid.
Sauté diced onion in lard or oil for 3–4 minutes until soft, add garlic for 1 minute, then bloom cumin, chili powder, and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add beans and 2 tbsp reserved liquid, simmer 2–3 minutes, and mash with a potato masher (adding extra liquid as needed) until creamy.

title: Copycat House Negi Shio Dare Addictive Cabbage
subtitle: Gram-accurate izakaya cabbage tossed with toasted sesame oil, chicken bouillon, garlic & negi
yieldText: 600g raw cabbage batch (drag Cabbage slider to match any cabbage head weight!)

ingredients.name: Fresh Green Cabbage Leaves (torn into 4–5cm squares)
Roasted White Sesame Seeds (いりごま 白)
Chicken Bouillon Granules (鶏がらスープの素)
Japanese Soy Sauce (濃口しょうゆ)

instructions: Wash and thoroughly dry cabbage leaves; tear into 4–5cm bite-sized squares.
Place a large mixing bowl on the kitchen scale, tare to 0.0g, and weigh all sesame oil and seasonings directly into the bowl. Whisk well.
Toss cabbage in 2–3 batches until evenly glossy, rest 5–10 minutes at room temp to lightly wilt, and serve.

title: Ultimate Crispy Beer-Battered Onion Rings & Comeback Sauce
subtitle: Sweet yellow onions in a light flour-cornstarch carbonated beer batter

ingredients.name: Vidalia or Sweet Yellow Onions (1/2" rings, membrane peeled)
Ice-Cold Beer (Lager, Pilsner, or Pale Ale)

instructions: Slice onions into 1/2-inch rounds, separate into rings, and peel off the thin inner papery membrane so the batter adheres.
Whisk flour, cornstarch, baking powder, and spices. Scoop out 60g (1/2 cup) onto a shallow plate for the dry dredge.
Whisk ice-cold beer into the remaining dry mix just until combined.
Coat onion rings in the reserved dry mix, dip in beer batter, and fry at 190°C (375°F) for 2–3 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain on a wire rack and salt immediately.

title: Classic Homemade Molcajete Guacamole
subtitle: Rustic Hass avocado guacamole built on a mashed onion-jalapeño-cilantro-salt paste
instructions: Mash diced white onion, minced jalapeño, half the cilantro, and coarse sea salt in a molcajete or bowl with the back of a fork to release aromatic oils.
Scoop in avocado flesh and coarsely mash into chunky bite-sized pieces.
Gently fold in fresh lime juice, seeded diced tomato, and remaining cilantro.

title: Air Fryer Crispy Spiced Okra
subtitle: 450g fresh okra tossed with garlic, smoked paprika, cornstarch crunch & lemon spritz
instructions: Rinse okra and pat completely dry with paper towels; trim stems.
Toss with oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and optional cornstarch.
Air-fry in a single layer at 200°C (390°F) for 10–12 minutes, shaking halfway, then spritz with fresh lemon juice.

title: Creamy Tomato Soup with Tempered Cream Cheese
subtitle: Velvety canned tomato puree soup enriched with tempered cream cheese & aromatics

ingredients.name: Bay Leaf, Dried Oregano & Fresh Basil

instructions: Sweat diced onion in 2 tbsp butter over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes until soft without browning.
Stir in garlic, herbs, and tomato paste for 60–90 seconds.
Add 775ml tomato puree, 350ml chicken broth, and bay leaf; simmer partially covered for 15–20 minutes.
Discard bay leaf and blend smooth with an immersion blender.
Temper softened cream cheese with 120ml warm soup in a small bowl until smooth, then whisk back into the pot.

title: Tataki Kyūri (Smashed Cucumber Salad)
subtitle: Crisp izakaya-style smashed cucumbers tossed in toasted sesame oil, soy sauce & rice vinegar

ingredients.name: Japanese Soy Sauce (濃口しょうゆ)
Toasted White Sesame Seeds (iri-goma / いりごま)
Chicken Bouillon Powder (鶏がらスープの素)

instructions: Place the trimmed cucumbers on a cutting board. Lightly whack them along their length with a rolling pin or the flat side of a chef's knife until they split open along their natural seams. Tear or cut into 2–3 cm (1-inch) bite-sized chunks so the rough, jagged edges can catch the dressing.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, and toasted sesame oil (along with optional grated garlic and chicken bouillon powder) until the sugar fully dissolves.

About 15–20 minutes before serving, toss the smashed cucumbers with the dressing and toasted white sesame seeds (plus optional rāyu). Keep chilled in the refrigerator until serving to maintain maximum crispness.
chefNotes: Smashing the cucumbers instead of cleanly slicing them creates craggy, fractured surfaces that allow the sesame-soy dressing to cling and infuse rapidly.
Toss and chill for 15–20 minutes right before serving. Dressing cucumbers too far in advance causes them to release excess water and lose their signature snappy crunch.

title: Old Fashioned Chocolate Chip Cookies (Gram-Weighed)
subtitle: Rich brown-sugar & butter cookies with 340g chocolate chips (Full & Half batch calibrated)
yieldText: 24 cookies at ~45g each (1,070.5g dough) — tap 12 cookies for your exact Half Recipe!
instructions: Cream softened butter, granulated sugar, and light brown sugar in a bowl until smooth.
Beat in eggs and vanilla extract completely.
Mix in baking soda and salt, then fold in flour just until combined.
Fold in chocolate chips, portion onto baking sheets according to your chosen cookie count and gram weight, and bake at 190°C (375°F) for ~12 minutes.

title: Nestlé Toll House Double Chocolate Brownies
subtitle: Fudgy 9"×9" pan brownies made with melted chocolate morsels plus studded chips & nuts

ingredients.name: Nestlé Semi-Sweet Chocolate Chips (divided)
ingredients.volumeText: 12 oz pkg (1 cup melted + 1 cup stirred in)

instructions: Preheat oven to 163°C (325°F). Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt in a small bowl.
In a small saucepan, bring butter, sugar, and 2 tbsp water just to a boil, then remove from heat.
Stir in 170g (1 cup) chocolate chips and vanilla extract until melted and smooth. Transfer to a large bowl and beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour mixture, then stir in the remaining 170g (1 cup) chocolate chips and nuts.
Spread in a greased 9-inch square pan and bake 30–35 minutes. Cool completely and cut into squares.

title: Mia & Daddy's Honey Lemonade
subtitle: Refreshing honey-sweetened fresh lemon juice pitcher or glass formula
instructions: Stir honey with a splash of warm water until dissolved, then mix with fresh lemon juice and cold water over ice.
